the carbon acceptor in GaAs and InGaAs grown by low-pressure MOCVD can be passivated by hydrogen, which can be incorporated during cool-down or during growth, and the degree of passivatation is affected by the cool-down sequence, and the presence of a cap layer and/or a P-doped layer.

the hole concentration in carbon-doped Ga1−yInyAs grown by MOCVD can be increased by annealing at ≈400°C in N2, and that hydrogen can be incorporated into the material from AsH3 and PH3, as well as from H2.
hydrogen passivation of C acceptors in GaAs and InGaAs grown by MOCVD is observed in the absence of a capping layer, and can be controlled by the choice of cool-down ambient.

the effects of hydrogen passivation on the electrical properties of carbon acceptors in GaAs, In0.53 Ga0.47As and HBT structures.

the effects of hydrogen on C-doped GaAs and InGaAs grown by MOCVD, and on the performance of HBTs grown by MOCPD.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrogen passivation of C in GaAs is more effective than in InGaAs and that the passivation is more severe in InGaAs than in InGaP.
the hydrogen passivation of C-acceptors in InP/In0.53Ga 0.47As HBTs is more significant and more difficult to remove than in the case of GaAs-based devices.

The main takeaway from our work is that
carbon-doped InP/InAlAs HBTs can be grown at low temperature with high carbon concentrations and high hole concentrations without the need for post-growth anneals.
carbon acceptors are passivated by hydrogen during the post-growth cool-down, and this effect must be considered when designing C-doped devices.
